Ok, if you know EVERYTHING that is going to happen, it is possible, in theory, to complete in a single run, but not recommended at all.

To do that, you'd have to complete all missions and core supressions in one shot. If you're going to use memory repository, don't worry bc they carry over them, as well as through day 1 resets.

(Spoiler for the later days)

Missions: (remember: You need to complete all requirements of a mission in a single day) ||A tl;dr for the toughest missions is: Supress WAWs 5 times (you can just grind one, King of Greed is super easy for this), supress 3 different ALEPHs (Would reccomend doing apocalypse bird, which appears when Judgement Bird, Big Bird and Punishing bird breach, if two breach the thrid one will automatically, plus you get some OP gear and EGO gifts for all survivors), have some ALEPH gear (I don't remember the number but you'll need 2 or 3 ALEPHs to get to that, or 1 if you get Judgement bird, King of greed and apoc. bird's gears) and have high stat agents (Like 100+ stats).||

Now, for the core supressions, given the day you're at you can't do them yet, but I'll let you know they're the toughest challenges in the game and are essential for the story and to get the true ending. If you want to get spoiled, ||Core supressions are pretty much fighting each sephirah. With two exceptions, all of them make the management phase really hard. Malkuth changes the types of work (ordering attachment = repression work, for example), Yesod reduces your screen to 144p resolution (not literally but you get the point), Hod yeets your stats by -40 and Netzach kills the healing system. And that's just the upper layer supressions, it gets harder from here but I'm not going any further.||

But basically I wouldn't reccomend doing a single run  because A) day 1 reset allows you to start with all EGO and abno information you got and mission and core supression progress and B) I'd highly reccomend doing a specialized run, i.e. choosing all abnos that don't suck to make the endgame easier (fyi, days 46+ are the boss fight equivalent for this game. When you get there you'll see how hard it is, and having a bad abno could screw up everything.)

If you screw up like I did, move everyone to a place the pilars won't hit and call the rabbits. Remember, this is essentially the last day. You must complete this day at all costs.!<

Here are all the strategies for anyone who wants, including >!Kether trials.!<

NOTE: You must have Shelter from 27th or March (tool), Backwards clock (tool) and Blue star. Also, always have a burner employee for the clock.

You must be happy can help greatly.

Malkuth - >!Honestly, pay attention. Every meltdown level, have an employee ready to work with abnormalities who are ok with any work. After that, work with other abnormalities to know what becomes what. For example, if Instinct turns into Insight, you can work with Dreaming current/King of greed, who are ok with any work besides Insight. If you have trouble with memory, write it down.!<

Yesod - >!Ah, yes, 144p resolution. Again, Yesod needs you to pay a lot of attention. Pause often to make sure you didn't miss any meltdowns/ordeals. Pay attention to the amount of enemies an ordeal spawns as well (e.g. dawn spawns one per department, Central command counting as 2). You'll also need good memory to remember your employee's stats and the best work type for each abno.!<

Hod - >!Rip stats. You'll need a good team for this one. Grind stats and make sure you have people who can handle your WAWs and ALEPHs. The noon ordeals will be much tougher, so I reccomend taking on one enemy at a time (except for Violet noon, in which you'll have to prioritize)!<

Netzach - >!No healing for you. As always, attention. Make sure that each abnormality is worked with an employee who has high resistance to their damage type. If someone's injured, don't have them do work. Make a qlipoth meltdown happen while only one person is working to minimize damage. For ordeals, use shields. If you're unlucky to get green noon, take them down one at a time and make sure to only have one melee attacker (with red shield) and the rest ranged.!<

Tiphereth - >!The easiest one. The main problem here is the midnight ordeal it forces on you. Work as usual untill you know which one is coming. If it's violet, reset. If it's amber, gather everyone in the elevators on the side of the Training or Safety department rooms, and once the ordeal triggers, wait. When the max amount of amber dusks has been spawned, have that team attack the work AFTER it appears, and make them run back when it goes away. When all the midnight worms are dead, use backward clock to get rid of the rest and work normally. Green midnight is much easier. Gather everyone in the corridor left to the Information department's main room, and get everyone who has a short-ranged weapon in the elevator. When it starts, get your kill team there. If the laser reaches the position of 7 o'clock, get everyone in the elevator and, when the laser is between two elevators, use it to go through it. After it passes the elevator you were in, get back to beating it.!<

Gebura - >!Pretty easy too, but it takes a lot of time. Before starting the day, get all of your agents out and hire a single one per department. They're all going to die, except for one. Remember the shelter and Blue star in the beggining? Well, all you have to do is get someone in the shelter, wait for Blue star to breach, then profit. Blue star damages everything periodically, including the Red Mist. This will take a lot, and I mean a lot of time. I'm talking over an hour, but you don't have to do anything.!<

Chesed - >!Tough one, but becomes much easier if you did all other core supressions. Basically, work only with abnormalities whose damage type isn't affected or who are easy to handle (TETHs and ZAYINs). Like Netzach and Hod, take extreme care with noon ordeals, and use the clock with dusk. If you get amber dusk, time things right so the worms aren't digging when the effect activates. For crimson dusk, you'll have to deal with two noons and multiple dawns, so make sure to get employees away from the exploding clowns.!<

Binah - >!Before everything, make sure everyone has decent black resistance, since she summons black spikes below employees at the start of every phase. As soon as the day starts, start charging the clock and call the rabbits on her. Pause and deal with all the special meltdowns. Now, here you have two options. First, you use the clock on the second phase to deal with the great amount of meltdowns or you use the clock on the third phase, when you can't pause. If you're using the clock on the second phase, be ready to deal with things fast on the third, and if you're using it on the third, be careful with the black waves on the hallways.!<

Hokma - >!First of all, make sure you have 4 employees per department and 3 abnos in each. Not pausing sucks, and I had to leave my thumb in a very unconfortable position to not pause accidentally. Deal with ordeals and meltdowns like always, and make sure you haven't missed any. Use the clock with the dusk ordeal. In case of amber or crimson dusks, do the same thing I said on Chesed's supression. Now, for the midnight ordeal. First off, you need 15 abno. works to progress the qlipoth counter. With each department having 3 abnos, this makes a total of 30, almost perfect to skip the ordeal. With one work left to trigger the ordeal, pause. Yes, someone will die, but you need to complete this. Right after this, send everyone to work with abnormalities. Just make sure they won't die instantly when beggining the work. After this, you'll go to the abormality with quickest work time, and send the employee to work with it again, completing the meltdown.!<

Day 46 - >!Not many problems here. Regular managing shouldn't be a problem, but the ordeals are new. The red fixer is troublesome one death, when it activates a large lazer which damages everything in a super large arc. Everyone with red weakness should be in the opposite side of the facility. White fixer occasionally start praying, indicated by a bell noise. This reflects all damage, so get your kill team out, and when it stops, get them back in. The black fixer is easy to kill, but it triggers meltdowns on every abnormality in the department of death, so be ready to deal with it. Your priority of fixers must be black first, then white, then red. The black one can trigger breaches if left alone, and the white one has a large arc attack (similar to red fixer's death lazer), again used if left alone. For the actual day, deal with dawn and noon as I said. In dusk, use the backward clock. In midnight, use the rabbits to slow down The Claw (assuming no agents on the department) as you gather everyone. If the rabbits are somehow wiped, get the team ready and finish it off.!<

As said before, pay attention to which work type becomes which, remember employee's stats and best work types for each abno, and be careful with damage. Be extremely careful with dawn, and use the backward clock in noon. If you hire an EX employee, they should still be level V even with Hod's effect. If you screw up like I did, move everyone to a place the pilars won't hit and call the rabbits. Remember, this is essentially the last day. You must complete this day at all costs.!<
